title: When the Escarpment Burns
premise: Riverboat captain Silas Voss, a man who reinvented himself after fleeing a war he refuses to name, salvages a chest bearing the seal of Vhalen—a nation erased from the maps—and finds it stuffed with proof that his old commander orchestrated the massacre that ended it. Hunted by both the commander's agents and Vhaleni exiles who need the chest to reclaim their homeland, Silas must choose between burying his past again or leading them over the Escarpment before the dry season's last winds give way to snow. Betrayals on the ridge force him to admit the truth: the family he found on the river matters more than the identity he's been hiding behind. In the end, Silas surrenders the chest to the exiles at the mountain pass, testifies to what he knows, and stays—anchored at last—to watch the first snow fall with the people who chose him anyway.
about_author: Sable Reyes is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight rivers before writing full-time. Their fiction blends hard-won river lore with stories about people outrunning their own histories.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Silas navigates a treacherous low-water stretch of the Alder River, establishing his skill, his crew's loyalty, and his habit of never staying anywhere long. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: restless competence masking avoidance—we learn he pays debts in towns he then abandons.

chapters.title: What the Dredge Brings Up
chapters.summary: After a storm, Silas and deckhand Wren salvage a waterlogged chest stamped with Vhalen's extinct seal. Inside: ledgers, letters, and orders signed by 'Commander Ashe.' Silas goes white and lies badly about why. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread—the past surfacing like a drowned body.

chapters.title: Passengers Who Don't Pay
chapters.summary: Two Vhaleni exiles, Ilsa and her teenage brother Tomas, beg passage, revealing they've tracked the chest for years. Silas refuses; Wren, sensing money and trouble, quietly considers otherwise. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: suspicion versus sympathy as the siblings' desperation humanizes the dead nation.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Agents of Commander Ashe burn a dockside warehouse searching for the chest, forcing Silas to flee upstream at night with the stowaway exiles aboard. He recognizes the agents' tactics—his own old unit's. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: hunted guilt; running is no longer optional.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren confronts Silas: she knows he recognized the seal, and she wants a share of whatever the chest is worth—or the truth. He gives her neither, fracturing their trust. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: betrayal's first crack in the found family.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Map
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals the chest contains land grants proving Vhalen's exile communities legally own territory now claimed by Ashe's patrons—if delivered before the winter council convenes beyond the Escarpment. The dry season has weeks left. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into urgency; the deadline is set.

chapters.title: The Last Landing
chapters.summary: Silas moors the boat permanently, sells it to cover supplies, and agrees to guide the group overland—an admission that stopping costs less than running. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment; grief for the river life he's surrendering.

chapters.title: Foothill Town, Unfriendly
chapters.summary: In the gateway town of Corren's Ford, the group discovers wanted posters describing Silas under his real name: Silas Vosk, Ashe's former lieutenant. Tomas sees them first and says nothing. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: the boy's crisis of loyalty—he needs Silas but now fears him.

chapters.title: Names We Bury
chapters.summary: Tomas confronts Silas privately on the trail; Silas admits who he was but swears he deserted before the massacre, not after. Ilsa overhears and goes cold. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: confession without absolution—the truth wounds even when offered freely.

chapters.title: The Switchback Road
chapters.summary: The party climbs into the Escarpment's lower canyons, racing a rival exile faction also seeking the chest—one willing to kill for it. A rockslide nearly claims Wren; Silas saves her. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grudging respect rekindled through shared danger.

chapters.title: Ashe's Voice
chapters.summary: Captured agents deliver an offer: Ashe will pay handsomely and pardon Silas if the chest is returned. That night Silas dreams of the massacre for the first time in years. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation and nightmare entwined—the price of going home to his old self.

chapters.title: High Camp
chapters.summary: Storm-delayed above the treeline, the group shares rationed food and stories; Ilsa describes Vhalen before it burned, and Silas realizes he remembers the same streets from the other side. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: fragile intimacy—grief shared across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Rival Faction
chapters.summary: The rival exiles ambush the camp at dawn. In the melee, Wren takes the chest and vanishes with it—her bargain finally cashed. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: shock and abandonment; the found family fractures visibly.

chapters.title: Cold Trail
chapters.summary: Silas reads Wren's tracks like river currents and leads Ilsa and Tomas up a frozen couloir, while the rival faction splits to hunt them. Frostbite, thin air, dwindling time. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grim determination—every skill he has bent toward one person.

chapters.title: Wren Alone
chapters.summary: Wren, hiding in a cave with the chest, discovers its final document: Ashe's order naming Silas Vosk as the officer who refused to fire—and was branded a traitor for it. She weeps. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: devastating reversal—she sold out the one innocent man.

chapters.title: The Couloir
chapters.summary: Silas reaches Wren's cave as the rival faction closes in; she returns the chest and confesses what she read. Together they hold the cave mouth until Ilsa and Tomas arrive. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: forgiveness asked and granted mid-battle—loyalty rebuilt on truth.

chapters.title: Ashe Himself
chapters.summary: Commander Ashe intercepts the party at a ridge saddle with his remaining agents, offering Silas restoration of rank and name in exchange for the chest. Silas publicly renounces him: 'My name is Voss now.' POV: Silas. Emotional beat: climax of identity—choosing the invented self because it was honestly earned.

chapters.title: Ridge Fight
chapters.summary: A brutal fight on the knife-edge ridge as the first snow begins; Tomas saves Silas's life, repaying every debt between them. Ashe falls into the gorge clutching nothing but his own commission papers. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: catharsis—the boy becomes the protector.

chapters.title: The Pass
chapters.summary: Exhausted and half-frozen, the four cross the pass and reach the winter council as the dry season officially ends. Ilsa presents the chest; the grants are ratified. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: triumph laced with sorrow—vindication for a nation that no longer exists.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Silas testifies before the council about the massacre, naming names, accepting their judgment. Some exiles turn away forever; others, including Ilsa, stay to hear him out. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: accountability without guarantee of grace.

chapters.title: First Snow
chapters.summary: The council releases Silas with no sentence but memory. Wren proposes they run freight over the new trade route the grants opened—by boat in summer, by sled in winter. The found family reforms around work instead of flight. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet joy; purpose replacing escape.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Spring returns to the Alder River. Silas pilots a new boat with Wren, Ilsa, and Tomas aboard, passing the sandbar where the chest surfaced. He doesn't look away this time. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: resolution—a man who kept moving finally stays, because home is now a crew, not an address.
